sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
கா அடியாரை என்று சொல்லியே
காவடி எடுத்து வந்தேன் கந்தசாமியே
sections.translit:
kA adiyArai endRu solliyE
kAvadi edutthu vandhEn kandhasAmiyE
sections.en: Skanda, I carried the wood pole all the way to you, with offerings tied on either end of the pole. I prayed the entire way for you to protect your devotees.

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
வேல் வெற்றி வேல் என்று சொல்லியே
படி மேல் படி ஏறி வந்தேன் பழனிச்சாமியே
sections.translit:
vEl vetRi vEl endRu solliyE
padi mEl padi ERi vandhEn pazhanicchAmiyE
sections.en: Oh Lord residing in Pazhani, I came chanting “victory to the spear” as I climbed the hills, one step at a time.

sections.label: Charanam
sections.ta:
பாலும் பழமும் பசுந்தயிரும் சந்தனமும்
நாலும் மேனி பட்டு நிதானமாய் நீராடி
நீறும் பட்டுமாய் நீ ஜொலிச்சு நிற்கையிலே
தீரும் வினை என்று நானும் நேர்ந்துகிட்டேன்
sections.translit:
pAlum pazhamum pasunthayirum chandanamum
nAlum mEni pattu nidhAnamAy nIRadi
nIRum pattumAy nI jolicchu niRkaiyilE
thIrum vinai endRu nAnum nErndhukittEn
sections.en: Muruga, you had a shower of milk, fruit, cow’s milk curd, and sandalwood paste. This was followed by a long, relaxing bath in purified water. Then you stood, dazzling in silk robes and sacred ash smeared on your forehead.  I took one look at you and prayed that you remove all my past and present sins.

notes: The pallavi of this song refers to the process of carrying a Kavadi to Muruga’s hilltop abodes. There is a legend associated with carrying a kavadi. Sage Aghasthiya was asked to proceed south by Siva. The sage, being a staunch devotee of Siva and Parvathi, did not want to leave his worship in the sacred Sivagiri and Sakthigiri hills of Kailash. He decided to move the altar to the South. He assigned the task of carrying the hills to the South to his disciple Idumban, a demon who survived Surapadman‘s war with Lord Muruga. Idumban and his wife Idumbi became devotees of Lord Muruga after the war, and accepted the task. After a prayer to Siva, Idumban obtained a strong pole or stick which was comparable in strength to Brahmma dhanda. Siva also sent many snakes from all eight directions. Idumban used the snakes as ropes and tied them to both ends of the pole and used the snakes to create the base of a scale. Utilizing the newly constructed kavadi, they hung the two hills on scales and carried them on their shoulders. When Idumban came close to Thiruavinankudi (a scriptural name for Palani), he felt very tired and put the kavadi down. He noticed a young boy on one of the hills and asked him to leave. The young lad had left his home, fighting with his parents and elder brother about a mango prize he did not win in a contest to go around the world. Yes, that was Muruga who had decided to find a home to reside in. Muruga was in a fighting mood and told Idumban that he would not budge from the hills. Muruga killed Idumban in the war that ensued. Idumbi realized that the young lad must be Muruga and begged him to bring Idumban back to life. Muruga granted her wish and blessed them both. Idumban wanted to stay there as a sentinel to the Palani Hills and begged Muruga to bless any devotee that travels up the hills, carrying a kavadi and making offerings to Muruga. Muruga also granted the couple another boon: anyone praying at Idumban’s shrine halfway up the hills will be treated as having prayed to Muruga himself and will receive the Lord's compassion.
